themes_detail.label: For-Hire Vehicle Surge
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints spiked to 23 this week, up 372% from the 4.9-per-week baseline over the prior 8 weeks, suggesting a sudden deterioration in Uber/Lyft traffic management or driver conduct in Sunnyside/Woodside.
evidence: 23 for-hire vehicle complaints THIS WEEK vs. 4.9 weekly average (z-score: 7.65, highest statistical spike)
372% increase represents the second-largest proportional spike in the dataset
No prior Reddit discussions or local news coverage, suggesting this is an emerging localized issue
reporting_angles: Interview residents and businesses about specific complaints (double-parking, reckless driving, congestion)
Request data from TLC on for-hire vehicle violations and driver complaints in CD 402 this week

themes_detail.label: Outdoor Dining Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Outdoor dining complaints jumped to 3 this week, up 1100% from a 0.2 weekly baseline, indicating emerging friction over restaurant sheds or street dining operations in the district.
evidence: 3 outdoor dining complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average (z-score: 6.35)
1100% spike suggests a discrete event or policy change triggering enforcement or resident backlash
Timing aligns with spring/warm weather reopening of outdoor venues
reporting_angles: Identify which restaurants or blocks are generating complaints (check 311 addresses)
Determine if a specific enforcement sweep or new outdoor dining policy triggered the spike

themes_detail.label: Park Noise Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints from parks in Sunnyside/Woodside jumped to 5 this week, up 567% from the 0.8 weekly baseline, suggesting overcrowding or unruly behavior at a specific park amenity.
evidence: 5 park noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly average (z-score: 6.43)
567% spike coincides with warming weather and likely increased park usage
Community board has requested new/expanded parks and amenities—potential saturation of existing facilities
reporting_angles: Site visit to identify which park(s) are generating complaints and observe usage patterns
Interview Parks Department and community board on park capacity and whether overcrowding is contributing

themes_detail.label: Litter Basket Service Gap
themes_detail.summary: Litter basket requests surged to 5 last week, up 1900% from a 0.2 weekly baseline, indicating residents are reporting inadequate trash receptacle infrastructure across the neighborhood.
evidence: 5 litter basket requests last week vs. 0.2 weekly average (z-score: 7.18)
1900% spike is the third-largest proportional increase in the dataset
Aligns with seasonal increase in foot traffic and outdoor activity
reporting_angles: Map the 311 complaints to identify which blocks/parks lack adequate trash bins
Contact Sanitation Department on their litter basket deployment plan for the district

themes_detail.label: Dead Tree Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Dead or dying tree complaints spiked to 4 last week, up 3100% from a 0.1 weekly baseline, suggesting environmental stress or disease affecting street trees across Sunnyside/Woodside.
evidence: 4 dead/dying tree complaints last week vs. 0.1 weekly average (z-score: 11.72, highest z-score in dataset)
3100% spike is the largest proportional increase observed
Community board has repeatedly requested capital funds for Parks Department, suggesting prior infrastructure gaps
reporting_angles: Work with Parks Department to identify the cause (drought stress, disease, poor maintenance)
Investigate whether recent weather events (freeze/thaw cycles, late-season snow) triggered tree decline
